smalldocs builds a website from a folder of Markdown pages and notebooks. A file `_smalldocs.yml` in
the folder holds the options of the site. smalldocs writes the site into the folder `_site`.

Each page of the site has a navbar at the top, a sidebar at the left and a table of contents at the
right. smalldocs also makes reference pages from your Python code, and pages that list other pages,
such as a blog.

A theme is a stylesheet that sets the colours and the fonts of the site. smalldocs includes the
[Bootswatch themes](https://bootswatch.com) and can install themes from a git repository.

This site uses Folio, with serif text, a monospace font for code, and light and dark modes.
[Choose and install a theme](guide/themes.qmd#themes-in-the-elegant-collection), or
[compare the themes](https://rahuldave.com/elegant-themes/).

smalldocs is one Python package, and it needs no other programs. Install it from PyPI:

```bash
pip install smalldocs
```

Build a site, or preview it while you write:

```bash
smalldocs render docs      # writes docs/_site
smalldocs preview docs     # serves it at http://127.0.0.1:4200 and reloads on every change
```

## What smalldocs does not do

smalldocs makes websites only. It does not make PDF files, Word files, slides or books. It does not
run code. A notebook shows the outputs that were saved in it.

## Where the conventions come from

smalldocs takes its conventions from [Quarto](https://quarto.org), a larger tool that also makes PDFs
and slides. The conventions are the `.qmd` pages, the Markdown of [Pandoc](https://pandoc.org), and the
options of a site. So a Quarto website builds with smalldocs, with no change. If you use Quarto now, read
[From Quarto](guide/from-quarto.qmd), and run `smalldocs check`.
